thread:
Maya (support): heads up — Acme reports outputs from parallel tool calls are being attributed to the wrong segments. started after last night's deploy. escalating.
Acme SRE: repro steps: POST /v1/generate with tools=[translate_v1, extract_topics]; we send 4 segments in one request, runtime fanouts two tool calls per segment in parallel. responses come back and some `tool_result` entries are assigned to other segment ids. happened on 2026-03-16 at ~22:03 UTC.
Maya (support): they attached a minimal payload, dropping it here.
Acme SRE: ```json
{
  "request_id": "req_0a1b2c3d",
  "segments": ["s1","s2","s3","s4"],
  "tools": ["translate_v1","topic_extractor_v2"],
  "debug": true
}
```
Acme SRE: observed response (trimmed):
```
{
  "request_id":"req_0a1b2c3d",
  "results":[
    {"segment":"s1","tool_result":{"tool":"translate_v1","text":"..."}},
    {"segment":"s2","tool_result":{"tool":"topic_extractor_v2","topics":[...] }},
    {"segment":"s3","tool_result":{"tool":"translate_v1","text":"(actually from s2)"}},
  ]
}
```
Acme SRE: note the translate output for s3 is clearly the translation for s2. also seeing doubled billing tokens for some segments.
Devon (eng-runtime): thanks, this sounds like an association/correlation bug in the multi-tool dispatcher. any chance you can share the call-level logs with `call_id` and `correlation_id`?
Acme SRE: attaching sample logs (sanitized) below.
Acme SRE: ```
[2026-03-16T22:03:12.123Z] call_id=ck1 dispatch segment=s2 tool=translate_v1 corr=cid-77a
[2026-03-16T22:03:12.125Z] call_id=ck2 dispatch segment=s3 tool=translate_v1 corr=cid-77b
[2026-03-16T22:03:12.210Z] result call_id=ck2 tool=translate_v1 corr=cid-77b status=ok
[2026-03-16T22:03:12.211Z] result call_id=ck1 tool=translate_v1 corr=cid-77a status=ok
[2026-03-16T22:03:12.215Z] aggregator attached result corr=cid-77b -> segment=s2
[2026-03-16T22:03:12.215Z] aggregator attached result corr=cid-77a -> segment=s3
```
Acme SRE: looks like aggregator used corr id ordering but corr ids are not monotonically tied to segment ordering. outputs got swapped.
ben (oncall): I'm taking this. initial hypothesis: race in the aggregator where we pop from a pending list by arrival order but then index into a segment array by an offset that assumes same ordering. if two tool calls complete near-simultaneously ordering can flip.
Devon (eng-runtime): that matches an older bug we patched in v2.12 but I thought we fixed the aggregator-indexing. deploy-bot: "deploy v2.14.3 completed 2026-03-16T21:45:00Z (autodeploy)"
deploy-bot: rollback available: v2.14.2
Alice (devex): can Acme confirm whether they used the batch `concurrent=true` flag or if this was implicit? helps narrow repro.
Acme SRE: they used `concurrent=true`. their client fanouts are fast (50ms between segment ops).
Ravi (sre): please attach heap/trace IDs for the runtime host. we need flame traces for the aggregator thread. also check if correlation_id generation changed in the last deploy.
Devon (eng-runtime): grabbing recent commits — there's a change in the dispatcher that reuses a per-request counter for corr ids when `concurrent=true`. I suspect duplicate corr ids across subcalls if counter is reset incorrectly. will add stricter uniqueness (uuid per subcall).
Maya (support): immediate action for customer: 1) offer to pause parallelization (workaround: concurrent=false) 2) offer credits for misbilled tokens 3) ETA for fix?
ben (oncall): repro plan: create a small harness that simulates 1000 multi-tool requests with concurrent=true and assert mapping between call_id/corr and segment; I can reproduce locally within ~30s. adding extra debug logs to aggregator to print mapping on attach.
Devon (eng-runtime): if we can reproduce, patch will be: make corr id = `${request_id}:${uuid.v4()}` and make aggregator match by call_id instead of arrival index. preparing a hotfix branch.
Alice (devex): I'll follow up with Acme on workaround instructions and collect a sanitized trace and request samples for SRE/Eng.
Maya (support): customer update posted: "we're investigating, you can set concurrent=false to avoid the issue. engineering is on it." :thumbsup:
Acme SRE: thanks. please keep me posted, we use this heavily in production so would prefer a hotfix over a permanent change in our client.
ben (oncall): timeline: repro + unit test (2h), patch + internal canary (4h), roll (1h) — if no regressions we can roll in next day window.
Devon (eng-runtime): start PR and tag me. i'll own review and can push canary.
Maya (support): adding ticket references and billing escalation so finance can review token charges.
Ravi (sre): after patch we should run synthetic tests stressing concurrent subcalls across different sequence lengths and ensure no tool_result re-association.
